findings.statement: SCARB1 is a surface protein (UniProt, SURFY and CSPA agree) but Human Protein Atlas staining is high in the adrenal gland, the kidney is stained at an intermediate level, and the GTEx proteome flags adrenal enrichment as an on-target off-tumour concern; only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1]. A conjugate would face a narrow window and the score does not show it would work.

CD70 is a single-pass surface protein and a known-target control; it scores well for conjugate suitability [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]. Human Protein Atlas staining data are not available for it, so normal-tissue safety rests on the GTEx proteome (not enriched in vital organs) and cannot be confirmed by immunohistochemistry here.

ENPP3 is a surface-confirmed control target (CSPA high confidence), but normal kidney is stained at the top level [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0]. Duodenum staining is also high, so on-target kidney and gut toxicity is the main concern for a conjugate.

CA9 is a control target with surface topology, but the GTEx proteome shows stomach enrichment above the safety threshold [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]. Kidney staining is none and CSPA did not observe it at the surface, so it remains a lead with a gastric on-target risk.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation (higher in mutants in CPTAC RNA, CPTAC protein and TCGA RNA) [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971]. It is not flagged for VHL, BAP1 or SETD2, and the CPTAC PBRM1 protein effect is modest.

PSAT1 is lower in tumours but higher in BAP1-mutant tumours, with the TCGA RNA difference given here [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711]. The CPTAC protein difference is not significant and it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate; it also tracks the ccB split, so it may mark an aggressive subtype rather than a driver-specific target.

PCK1 does not differ by VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 mutation at the protein level, but its RNA is lower in ccB than ccA [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581]. The CPTAC protein ccB difference is not significant, so the subtype link is RNA-level only.

In IMmotion150, higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib but not significantly [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336]. The combination versus sunitinib difference is not significant after correction [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917], and the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial shows no difference either; this is a lead from a small arm, not a predictor.

For NNMT the tool returned only the nivolumab trials (no IMmotion150 arms), so the combination versus sunitinib question cannot be answered. In the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial higher NNMT is weakly associated with earlier progression on nivolumab and the difference between the drugs is null after correction [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.083].

Higher PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab in IMmotion150 [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=0.22], but this is not significant after correction, the arm difference is also null, and the direction flips in other arms. PCK1 is therefore a prognostic-style marker in tumours, not a treatment-selection marker on this evidence.

For EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) only the nivolumab trials were returned; higher expression is associated with longer benefit on everolimus and nivolumab in the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial, with no significant difference between the drugs after correction. Neither that trial nor the very small Choueiri nivolumab trial supports using it to choose between these treatments.

Most of CD70 tumour transcripts come from immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it correlates positively with CD8 T cells and regulatory T cells. It is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383], an association only (no adjusted p-value quoted here), so a conjugate would also hit infiltrating lymphocytes.

SLC16A3 shows a large immune-cell share of its tumour transcripts [gene=SLC16A3; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.667], with essentially no correlation with CD8 T cells. It is not a strong immune target and its tumour signal needs the single-cell check, which is discordant between datasets.

The cell attribution of SCARB1 does not hold between single-cell datasets: myeloid cells dominate in the Li dataset but tumour cells in the Zhang dataset, with a modest share-profile correlation [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336]. Tumour-over-tubule enrichment is positive in both, but only four paired donors support the Zhang dataset.

NNMT is the cleanest cell attribution: tumour cells dominate in both the Li and Zhang datasets [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97], with the highest share-profile agreement of the genes checked. Both datasets show strong tumour-over-tubule enrichment, though the Zhang comparison rests on four paired donors.

The cell attribution of SLC16A3 is not stable: T and NK cells dominate in the Li dataset whereas tumour cells dominate in the Zhang dataset, and the dominant group differs. Tumour-over-tubule enrichment is strongly positive in both datasets, so tumour expression is plausible but the cell-of-origin call is unresolved.

SCARB1 protein is higher in tumours in the independent label-free cohort and the call replicates [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334]. Replication of direction and significance supports a tumour-up protein, not conjugate suitability.

PSAT1 protein loss in tumours replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. One phosphosite was measurable in both cohorts and significant in discovery, but it did not replicate.

NNMT protein is strongly higher in tumours in the confirmatory cohort and replicates [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]. The fold change differs from discovery because the technology differs; direction and significance are what count.

SLC16A3 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory cohort and replicates [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]. Its one shared phosphosite also replicates.

caveats: Treatment-response associations come from one trial with small arms or small nivolumab cohorts; none differs between arms after correction, so they are leads, not predictors.
A high ADC suitability score does not show a conjugate would work; CD70 lacks Human Protein Atlas staining data, and CA9 and SCARB1 show vital-organ proteome enrichment.
Single-cell attribution rests on two datasets with few paired donors; SCARB1 and SLC16A3 disagree between them.

PSAT1 and PCK1 are down in tumours, so they are biomarkers rather than targets; EPAS1, ENPP3 and PCK1 are covered only for some layers because of the tool-call budget; PNCK, FABP6, CYP2J2 and other ranked genes were not profiled.
Treatment records for NNMT and EPAS1 contained no IMmotion150 arms.
